source: Hand-curated Sino-Japanese / Sino-Korean cognate pairs — words sharing the same Chinese root, explained in English.
notes: Roughly 60% of Japanese and Korean vocabulary comes from the same Classical Chinese roots, so a huge number of words are cognates — they sound similar because the Japanese on'yomi and the Korean Hanja reading descend from the same source. This deck pairs common Japanese words with their Korean cognate (in Hangul + Revised Romanization) and points out the regular sound correspondences. The Japanese word is the study front; the English meaning and the Korean comparison are on the back. A handful of 'pattern' cards explain recurring morpheme correspondences (無→무, 学→학, 国→국, etc.) that let you predict cognates you've never seen. Useful if you study (or want to start) both languages.

cards.context: Korean: 무료 (muryo). Almost identical. The 無 (mu, 'non-/free of') prefix maps regularly: Japanese 無 = Korean 무 (mu). Learn this one and you can predict 無理/무리, 無視/무시.
cards.example_sentence: 入場は無料です。
cards.example_reading: にゅうじょう は むりょう です。
cards.example_meaning: Admission is free.

cards.context: Korean: 무리 (muri). Essentially the same word and meaning — 'unreasonable / pushing too hard.' 무리하지 마 = 無理しないで (don't overdo it). The 無 = 무 pattern again.
cards.example_sentence: そんなに働くと体に無理がある。
cards.example_reading: そんなに はたらく と からだ に むり が ある。
cards.example_meaning: Working that much is too hard on your body.

cards.context: Korean: 무시 (musi). 무시하다 = 無視する (to ignore). 無 (mu) = 무, 視 (shi) = 시 (si). Note Japanese し often = Korean 시 (si).
cards.example_sentence: 彼は私の話を無視した。
cards.example_reading: かれ は わたし の はなし を むし した。
cards.example_meaning: He ignored what I said.

cards.context: Korean: 약속 (yaksok) — one of the most strikingly similar cognates. 약속하다 = 約束する (to promise). 約 (yaku) = 약 (yak), 束 (soku) = 속 (sok).
cards.example_sentence: 友達と映画の約束をした。
cards.example_reading: ともだち と えいが の やくそく を した。
cards.example_meaning: I made plans to see a movie with a friend.

cards.context: Korean: 준비 (junbi) — nearly identical. 준비하다 = 準備する (to prepare). 準 (jun) = 준 (jun), 備 (bi) = 비 (bi).
cards.example_sentence: 旅行の準備をしている。
cards.example_reading: りょこう の じゅんび を して いる。
cards.example_meaning: I'm getting ready for a trip.

cards.context: Korean: 온도 (ondo) — identical in sound. 温 (on) = 온 (on), 度 (do) = 도 (do). The 度 = 도 (do) mapping shows up in 制度/제도, 態度/태도.
cards.example_sentence: 部屋の温度を下げた。
cards.example_reading: へや の おんど を さげた。
cards.example_meaning: I lowered the room temperature.

cards.context: Korean: 도로 (doro) — almost the same. 道 (dō) = 도 (do), 路 (ro) = 로 (ro). Japanese long ō frequently shortens to a plain Korean vowel.
cards.example_sentence: この道路は夜とても静かだ。
cards.example_reading: この どうろ は よる とても しずか だ。
cards.example_meaning: This road is very quiet at night.

cards.context: Korean: 고속도로 (gosokdoro) — a whole phrase that's nearly identical. 高速 = 고속 (gosok), 道路 = 도로 (doro). String the cognates together and full compounds line up.
cards.example_sentence: 高速道路で渋滞に巻き込まれた。
cards.example_reading: こうそく どうろ で じゅうたい に まきこまれた。
cards.example_meaning: I got caught in a traffic jam on the expressway.

cards.context: Korean: 기억 (gieok). 기억하다 = 記憶する (to memorize/remember). 記 (ki) = 기 (gi), 憶 (oku) = 억 (eok).
cards.example_sentence: 子供の頃の記憶はあいまいだ。
cards.example_reading: こども の ころ の きおく は あいまい だ。
cards.example_meaning: My childhood memories are hazy.

cards.context: Korean: 가구 (gagu). 家 (ka) = 가 (ga), 具 (gu) = 구 (gu). Note Japanese voiceless k often = Korean voiced g at the start of a word.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい家具を買いそろえた。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい かぐ を かいそろえた。
cards.example_meaning: I bought a full set of new furniture.

cards.context: Korean: 가족 (gajok). 家 (ka) = 가 (ga), 族 (zoku) = 족 (jok). Japanese ぞ/zo often = Korean 조 (jo).
cards.example_sentence: 家族と一緒に夕食を食べた。
cards.example_reading: かぞく と いっしょ に ゆうしょく を たべた。
cards.example_meaning: I had dinner with my family.

cards.context: Korean: 기분 (gibun). 기분 좋다 = 気分がいい (feel good). 気 (ki) = 기 (gi), 分 (bun) = 분 (bun). A word you'll hear constantly in both languages.
cards.example_sentence: 散歩したら気分がよくなった。
cards.example_reading: さんぽ したら きぶん が よく なった。
cards.example_meaning: I felt better after taking a walk.

cards.context: Korean: 간단 (gandan). 간단하다 = 簡単だ (to be simple). 簡 (kan) = 간 (gan), 単 (tan) = 단 (dan). Japanese ん before t/d = Korean ㄴ (n).
cards.example_sentence: この問題は簡単だ。
cards.example_reading: この もんだい は かんたん だ。
cards.example_meaning: This problem is easy.

cards.context: Korean: 만족 (manjok). 만족하다 = 満足する (to be satisfied). 満 (man) = 만 (man), 足 (zoku) = 족 (jok). Same 족 ending as 家族/가족.
cards.example_sentence: 結果に満足している。
cards.example_reading: けっか に まんぞく して いる。
cards.example_meaning: I'm satisfied with the result.

cards.context: Korean: 유명 (yumyeong). 유명하다 = 有名だ (to be famous). 有 (yū) = 유 (yu), 名 (mei) = 명 (myeong). Japanese 〜めい/mei often = Korean 〜명 (myeong).
cards.example_sentence: この店は有名なラーメン屋だ。
cards.example_reading: この みせ は ゆうめい な ラーメンや だ。
cards.example_meaning: This place is a famous ramen shop.

cards.context: Korean: 위험 (wiheom). 위험하다 = 危険だ (to be dangerous). Less obvious by sound, but the same 危険 root. 険 (ken) = 험 (heom).
cards.example_sentence: 夜の山道は危険だ。
cards.example_reading: よる の やまみち は きけん だ。
cards.example_meaning: Mountain paths are dangerous at night.

cards.context: Korean: 단순 (dansun). 단순하다 = 単純だ (to be simple). 単 (tan) = 단 (dan), 純 (jun) = 순 (sun).
cards.example_sentence: 考え方が単純すぎる。
cards.example_reading: かんがえかた が たんじゅん すぎる。
cards.example_meaning: That way of thinking is too simplistic.

cards.context: Korean: 긴장 (ginjang). 긴장하다 = 緊張する (to get nervous). 緊 (kin) = 긴 (gin), 張 (chō) = 장 (jang). Japanese 〜ちょう/chō often = Korean 〜장 (jang).
cards.example_sentence: 面接の前はとても緊張した。
cards.example_reading: めんせつ の まえ は とても きんちょう した。
cards.example_meaning: I was very nervous before the interview.

cards.context: Korean: 운동 (undong). 운동하다 = 運動する (to exercise). 運 (un) = 운 (un), 動 (dō) = 동 (dong). Japanese 〜どう/dō often = Korean 〜동 (dong).
cards.example_sentence: 健康のために毎日運動している。
cards.example_reading: けんこう の ため に まいにち うんどう して いる。
cards.example_meaning: I exercise every day for my health.

cards.context: Korean: 계산 (gyesan). 계산하다 = 計算する (to calculate); also means 'paying the bill' in Korean restaurants. 計 (kei) = 계 (gye), 算 (san) = 산 (san).
cards.example_sentence: 暗算で計算した。
cards.example_reading: あんざん で けいさん した。
cards.example_meaning: I calculated it in my head.

cards.context: Korean: 계획 (gyehoek). 계획하다 = 計画する (to plan). 計 (kei) = 계 (gye), 画 (kaku) = 획 (hoek). The 計 = 계 (gye) mapping also gives 計算/계산.
cards.example_sentence: 週末の計画を立てた。
cards.example_reading: しゅうまつ の けいかく を たてた。
cards.example_meaning: I made plans for the weekend.

cards.context: Korean: 습관 (seupgwan). 습관 = 習慣 (habit). 習 (shū) = 습 (seup), 慣 (kan) = 관 (gwan). The 〜慣/館/官 = 관 (gwan) mapping is very productive.
cards.example_sentence: 早起きの習慣をつけたい。
cards.example_reading: はやおき の しゅうかん を つけたい。
cards.example_meaning: I want to develop the habit of waking up early.

cards.context: Korean: 감사 (gamsa). 감사합니다 = a formal 'thank you' (= 感謝します). 感 (kan) = 감 (gam), 謝 (sha) = 사 (sa). Japanese ん before s = Korean ㅁ (m) here.
cards.example_sentence: ご協力に感謝します。
cards.example_reading: ご きょうりょく に かんしゃ します。
cards.example_meaning: Thank you for your cooperation.

cards.context: Korean: 초대 (chodae). 초대하다 = 招待する (to invite). 招 (shō) = 초 (cho), 待 (tai) = 대 (dae). Note Japanese し/しょ can map to Korean ㅊ (ch).
cards.example_sentence: 結婚式に招待された。
cards.example_reading: けっこんしき に しょうたい された。
cards.example_meaning: I was invited to a wedding.

cards.context: Korean: 결혼 (gyeolhon). 결혼하다 = 結婚する (to marry). 結 (ke[k]) = 결 (gyeol), 婚 (kon) = 혼 (hon). Japanese small っ (gemination) often corresponds to a Korean ㄹ (l) final.
cards.example_sentence: 二人は来年結婚する。
cards.example_reading: ふたり は らいねん けっこん する。
cards.example_meaning: The two of them will marry next year.

cards.context: Korean: 요리 (yori). 요리하다 = 料理する (to cook). 料 (ryō) = 요 (yo), 理 (ri) = 리 (ri). Japanese word-initial り/りょ = Korean 이/요 (the r/l is dropped at the start in Korean).
cards.example_sentence: 母の料理が一番おいしい。
cards.example_reading: はは の りょうり が いちばん おいしい。
cards.example_meaning: My mother's cooking is the best.

cards.context: Korean: 사진 (sajin). 사진 찍다 = 写真を撮る (take a photo). 写 (sha) = 사 (sa), 真 (shin) = 진 (jin).
cards.example_sentence: 旅行先でたくさん写真を撮った。
cards.example_reading: りょこうさき で たくさん しゃしん を とった。
cards.example_meaning: I took lots of photos at my travel destination.

cards.context: Korean: 주의 (juui). 注 (chū) = 주 (ju), 意 (i) = 의 (ui). Japanese ちゅ/chu = Korean 주 (ju). Signs in both countries warn with this word.
cards.example_sentence: 足元に注意してください。
cards.example_reading: あしもと に ちゅうい して ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please watch your step.

cards.context: Korean: 안전 (anjeon). 안전하다 = 安全だ (to be safe). 安 (an) = 안 (an), 全 (zen) = 전 (jeon). Japanese 〜ぜん/zen = Korean 〜전 (jeon).
cards.example_sentence: 安全のためヘルメットをかぶる。
cards.example_reading: あんぜん の ため ヘルメット を かぶる。
cards.example_meaning: Wear a helmet for safety.

cards.context: Korean: 도시 (dosi). 都 (to) = 도 (do), 市 (shi) = 시 (si). The 市 = 시 (si) mapping is everywhere (市場/시장, 市民/시민).
cards.example_sentence: 大都市の生活は便利だ。
cards.example_reading: だいとし の せいかつ は べんり だ。
cards.example_meaning: Life in a big city is convenient.

cards.context: Korean: 도서관 (doseogwan). 図書 (tosho) = 도서 (doseo), 館 (kan) = 관 (gwan). The 〜館 = 관 (gwan) ending recurs in 体育館/체육관, 大使館/대사관.
cards.example_sentence: 図書館で試験勉強をした。
cards.example_reading: としょかん で しけん べんきょう を した。
cards.example_meaning: I studied for the exam at the library.

cards.context: Korean: 공원 (gongwon). 公 (kō) = 공 (gong), 園 (en) = 원 (won). The 公 = 공 (gong) mapping gives 公共/공공, 公務員/공무원.
cards.example_sentence: 公園を散歩するのが日課だ。
cards.example_reading: こうえん を さんぽ する の が にっか だ。
cards.example_meaning: Walking in the park is my daily routine.

cards.context: Korean: 병원 (byeongwon). 病 (byō) = 병 (byeong), 院 (in) = 원 (won). Same 〜院 = 원 (won) as 大学院/대학원.
cards.example_sentence: 風邪をひいて病院に行った。
cards.example_reading: かぜ を ひいて びょういん に いった。
cards.example_meaning: I caught a cold and went to the hospital.

cards.context: Korean: 은행 (eunhaeng). Less obvious by sound but the same 銀行 root. 銀 (gin) = 은 (eun), 行 (kō) = 행 (haeng).
cards.example_sentence: 銀行で口座を開いた。
cards.example_reading: ぎんこう で こうざ を ひらいた。
cards.example_meaning: I opened an account at the bank.

cards.context: Korean: 교실 (gyosil). 教 (kyō) = 교 (gyo), 室 (shitsu) = 실 (sil). The 教 = 교 (gyo) mapping gives 教育/교육, 教会/교회.
cards.example_sentence: 教室はとても静かだった。
cards.example_reading: きょうしつ は とても しずか だった。
cards.example_meaning: The classroom was very quiet.

cards.context: Korean: 학생 (haksaeng). 学 (gaku) = 학 (hak), 生 (sei) = 생 (saeng). The 学 = 학 (hak) and 生 = 생 (saeng) mappings are two of the most useful to know.
cards.example_sentence: 私は日本語の学生です。
cards.example_reading: わたし は にほんご の がくせい です。
cards.example_meaning: I am a student of Japanese.

cards.context: Korean: 선생 (seonsaeng), politely 선생님 (seonsaengnim). 先 (sen) = 선 (seon), 生 (sei) = 생 (saeng). Same 生 = 생 as 学生/학생.
cards.example_sentence: 日本語の先生はとても優しい。
cards.example_reading: にほんご の せんせい は とても やさしい。
cards.example_meaning: My Japanese teacher is very kind.

cards.context: Korean: 시간 (sigan). 時 (ji) = 시 (si), 間 (kan) = 간 (gan). The 間 = 간 (gan) mapping gives 空間/공간, 人間/인간.
cards.example_sentence: 時間がないので急ごう。
cards.example_reading: じかん が ない ので いそごう。
cards.example_meaning: We're out of time, let's hurry.

cards.context: Korean: 과거 (gwageo). 過 (ka) = 과 (gwa), 去 (ko) = 거 (geo). Pairs with 未来/미래 and 現在/현재.
cards.example_sentence: 過去のことは忘れよう。
cards.example_reading: かこ の こと は わすれよう。
cards.example_meaning: Let's forget about the past.

cards.context: Korean: 미래 (mirae). 未 (mi) = 미 (mi), 来 (rai) = 래 (rae). Japanese らい/rai = Korean 래 (rae).
cards.example_sentence: 明るい未来を信じている。
cards.example_reading: あかるい みらい を しんじて いる。
cards.example_meaning: I believe in a bright future.

cards.context: Korean: 현재 (hyeonjae). 現 (gen) = 현 (hyeon), 在 (zai) = 재 (jae). Japanese げん/gen = Korean 현 (hyeon), as in 現実/현실.
cards.example_sentence: 現在の状況を説明します。
cards.example_reading: げんざい の じょうきょう を せつめい します。
cards.example_meaning: I'll explain the current situation.

cards.context: Korean: 자유 (jayu). 自 (ji) = 자 (ja), 由 (yū) = 유 (yu). The 自 = 자 (ja) mapping gives 自動/자동, 自然/자연.
cards.example_sentence: 言論の自由は大切だ。
cards.example_reading: げんろん の じゆう は たいせつ だ。
cards.example_meaning: Freedom of speech is important.

cards.context: Korean: 사회 (sahoe). 社 (sha) = 사 (sa), 会 (kai) = 회 (hoe). The 会 = 회 (hoe) mapping gives 会社/회사 (note the reversal!), 会議/회의.
cards.example_sentence: 現代社会は変化が速い。
cards.example_reading: げんだい しゃかい は へんか が はやい。
cards.example_meaning: Modern society changes quickly.

cards.context: Korean: 경제 (gyeongje). 経 (kei) = 경 (gyeong), 済 (zai) = 제 (je). Japanese けい/kei often = Korean 경 (gyeong), as in 경찰/警察.
cards.example_sentence: 世界経済が不安定だ。
cards.example_reading: せかい けいざい が ふあんてい だ。
cards.example_meaning: The world economy is unstable.

cards.context: Korean: 정부 (jeongbu). 政 (sei) = 정 (jeong), 府 (fu) = 부 (bu). Japanese せい/sei = Korean 정 (jeong), as in 정치/政治.
cards.example_sentence: 政府は新しい政策を発表した。
cards.example_reading: せいふ は あたらしい せいさく を はっぴょう した。
cards.example_meaning: The government announced a new policy.

cards.context: Korean: 문화 (munhwa). 文 (bun) = 문 (mun), 化 (ka) = 화 (hwa). The 化 = 화 (hwa) mapping gives 変化/변화, 文化/문화.
cards.example_sentence: 日本の文化に興味がある。
cards.example_reading: にほん の ぶんか に きょうみ が ある。
cards.example_meaning: I'm interested in Japanese culture.

cards.context: Korean: 역사 (yeoksa). 歴 (reki) = 역 (yeok), 史 (shi) = 사 (sa). Japanese word-initial れ/re drops to a vowel in Korean (역, no r).
cards.example_sentence: 日本の歴史を勉強している。
cards.example_reading: にほん の れきし を べんきょう して いる。
cards.example_meaning: I'm studying Japanese history.

cards.context: Korean: 국가 (gukga). 国 (ko[k]) = 국 (guk), 家 (ka) = 가 (ga). The 国 = 국 (guk) mapping gives 韓国/한국, 国民/국민, 外国/외국.
cards.example_sentence: 国家の安全を守る。
cards.example_reading: こっか の あんぜん を まもる。
cards.example_meaning: To protect the nation's security.

cards.context: Korean: 지도 (jido). 地 (chi) = 지 (ji), 図 (zu) = 도 (do). The 地 = 지 (ji) mapping gives 地下/지하, 地震/지진.
cards.example_sentence: 地図を見ながら歩いた。
cards.example_reading: ちず を みながら あるいた。
cards.example_meaning: I walked while looking at a map.

cards.context: Korean: 삼각 (samgak). 三 (san) = 삼 (sam), 角 (kaku) = 각 (gak). Japanese ん before k = Korean ㅁ (m) here. (삼각김밥 = the triangular convenience-store rice ball!)
cards.example_sentence: 三角の形に切ってください。
cards.example_reading: さんかく の かたち に きって ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please cut it into a triangle shape.

cards.context: Korean: 기차 (gicha) — and in Korean this is the everyday word for 'train'! 汽 (ki) = 기 (gi), 車 (sha) = 차 (cha). Note Japanese しゃ/sha = Korean 차 (cha).
cards.example_sentence: 昔は汽車で旅をした。
cards.example_reading: むかし は きしゃ で たび を した。
cards.example_meaning: Long ago, people traveled by steam train.

cards.context: PATTERN CARD. Japanese 無 (mu) = Korean 무 (mu), the negation prefix. Once you know it, you can guess: 無料/무료 (free), 無理/무리 (impossible), 無視/무시 (ignore), 無料/무료, 無責任/무책임 (irresponsible). Many Sino prefixes map this cleanly.
cards.example_sentence: 無料、無理、無視 — all start with 無 = 무.
cards.example_reading: むりょう、 むり、 むし。
cards.example_meaning: Free, impossible, ignore — all share the 無/무 prefix.

cards.context: PATTERN CARD. Japanese 学 (gaku) = Korean 학 (hak). Predicts: 学生/학생 (student), 学校/학교 (school), 大学/대학 (university), 学習/학습 (learning), 科学/과학 (science). A Japanese 〜く/ku ending often becomes a Korean ㄱ (k) final consonant.
cards.example_sentence: 学生、学校、大学 — 学 = 학。
cards.example_reading: がくせい、 がっこう、 だいがく。
cards.example_meaning: Student, school, university — all share 学/학.

cards.context: PATTERN CARD. Japanese 国 (koku) = Korean 국 (guk). Predicts: 韓国/한국 (Korea), 国民/국민 (citizens), 外国/외국 (foreign country), 国家/국가 (nation), 中国/중국 (China). Another 〜く/ku → ㄱ (k) final.
cards.example_sentence: 韓国、中国、外国 — 国 = 국。
cards.example_reading: かんこく、 ちゅうごく、 がいこく。
cards.example_meaning: Korea, China, foreign country — all share 国/국.

cards.context: PATTERN CARD. Japanese 〜館 (kan) = Korean 〜관 (gwan), a 'hall/building' suffix. Predicts: 図書館/도서관 (library), 体育館/체육관 (gym), 大使館/대사관 (embassy), 映画館/영화관 (cinema). The same 관 also covers 慣 (習慣/습관) and 官 (官僚/관료).
cards.example_sentence: 図書館、体育館、大使館 — 〜館 = 〜관。
cards.example_reading: としょかん、 たいいくかん、 たいしかん。
cards.example_meaning: Library, gym, embassy — all end in 館/관.
